description: The pocket can be a router. A name, a key, the laptop joins. The bundle pays. Heat and battery follow. Switch it off when the sitting ends.

title: The pivot table, properly
description: One thousand rows in, three sentences out, without touching a formula: select, drag, read. The spreadsheet's most respected tool, walked slowly in the series voice.

title: The portfolio: proof over promises
description: A CV says you can; a portfolio shows you did; a client decides in one glance. How to build the small body of evidence that turns every trade in this chapter into a living.

title: The profile that finds work
description: The employer searches your name before the handshake. A CV in Drive, a photograph that is your face, one honest profile, and the two sentences that make an application yours.

title: The Recycle Bin and “I deleted it”
description: Delete is a cupboard, not a fire. Restore puts the file back. Empty is the real goodbye. Shift+Delete skipped the cupboard — look twice.

title: The repairs engineer and the bench
description: Taking your laptop to a commercial workshop in town. The photographic inventory, serial numbers, password rules, agreed diagnostic bounds, and asking for old parts back in your hand.

title: The ride that comes to you
description: Bolt, Uber, inDrive — the street's bargaining, arranged neatly on a map. The plate, the PIN, the person told, and the driver who asks you to cancel answered politely and refused.

title: The right-click menu is a map
description: The right button is not a second click. It is a list of extra acts for whatever is under the pointer. Open, Rename, Delete, Open with, Properties. Click empty space to dismiss it.

title: The road ahead
description: From the first sitting to this one: the whole map on one page, the ten-year view, and the quiet hour you now owe somebody else. The last lesson of the series, and the first of yours.

title: The router and its five lights
description: Blinking is talking. The small lights on the shelf tell you exactly where the road is broken, and the restart has an order. Read the box before you call anybody.

title: The second lock
description: A stolen password should not be enough to be you. Two-step verification, backup codes on paper, and the rule for prompts you did not start.

title: A small network for a small shop
description: Router, POS, camera, printer, two laptops: draw the map before you buy anything. Power for the shelf, a guest gate for customers, and the book of passwords on the last page.

title: The room that never sleeps: the SOC
description: You will hear people say they work in a SOC. Here is the room, the tiers, the shifts — the place where the watching profession actually sits, explained without the mystique.

title: The upgrade habit
description: Every tool on this shelf will be replaced someday, and none of the habits will. The yearly skills audit, one new tool per quarter, unlearning with grace — how to stay current for decades.

title: The voice that borrowed a face
description: A clone needs twenty seconds of somebody's voice. The family word, the callback on the known number, and the rule that survives every costume: hurry, secrecy, money — pause.

title: The VPN, explained like a tunnel
description: Your traffic, wrapped and carried through another town: what a VPN actually does, when it genuinely helps, when it sells you courage — and why the free ones are the most expensive.

title: The webcam and who can see you
description: The camera is a hole at the top of the screen. A light means it is looking. A cover is a curtain. Off in the meeting is not the same as a closed curtain.

title: The working life
description: The last note of the chapter is about the years: routines that survive motivation, integrity that survives temptation, and a career walked one honest Thursday at a time.

title: When to say this is beyond me
description: The mark of a real technician is the sentence the amateur cannot say. Where your hands must stop, how to refer well, and why the honesty compounds faster than the luck.

title: Two windows at once
description: A letter on the left, a page on the right. Snap is not magic. Alt+Tab is the other door. You do not have to close one room to stand in the other.

title: Undo, and the thing you did not mean
description: Ctrl+Z takes back the last act. Ctrl+Y puts it back. Save is still the floor. Undo is a rope, not a time machine, and it dies when you close the window.

title: Uninstalling what a shop added
description: Settings, Apps, the name you do not remember asking for. Uninstall is showing a guest the door. The Start menu is not the same as gone.

title: Updates without panic
description: The restart is not a punishment. Save first, plug in the charger, let the bar finish. An update is a repair the machine already knows how to fetch.

title: Upgrading RAM: the honest math
description: A friend shouts that you need sixteen gigabytes of RAM to make your computer fast. Reading the numbers before spending money, the study desk rule, and the soldered chip trap.

title: USB devices that are not flash drives
description: The same hole takes a mouse, a keyboard, a printer, a dongle. Plug in, wait, look at the lights. The computer usually knows the guest. You still have to seat the plug.

title: Volume and headphones
description: Sound has a tap on the keyboard and a tap in the tray. Headphones steal the speakers until you unplug them. Mute is a line through the speaker, not a broken machine.

title: The vulnerability assessment: checking the fence
description: A vulnerability assessment is the systematic walk around your own walls before thieves do it for you — find the weak boards, rank them, fix the loudest first. Here is the honest method.

title: Watching a video without getting lost
description: A video site is a market with a search box. Type the thing you came for. Full screen is not a new street. The sidebar is a stall shouting. You may leave.

title: Water, tea, and the spill on the keyboard
description: The mug tips, tea floods the keys, and panic takes over. The immediate five-second drill: pull the plug, hold the button, the upside-down tent, and why raw rice ruins machines.

title: Websites for small businesses: a trade you can start this year
description: Every shop, school and church needs one honest page on the internet — and somebody local to build and keep it. That somebody can be you, from skills this shelf has already begun.

title: What a megabyte is, and where your data goes
description: A megabyte is a cup of water from a tank you paid for. Video drinks buckets, mail drinks cups, and the meter in Settings names every thirsty guest in the house.

title: What a PDF is for
description: A PDF is a photograph of a page that still lets you select the words. It will not rearrange itself on another computer. That is why offices ask for it.

title: What a QR code is doing
description: A QR code is a printed address. The camera reads it and offers a door. Read the door before you walk. A sticker on a pole is not your bank.

title: What “the computer has a virus” usually is
description: A flashing count of infections is usually an advert. A real problem is quieter: a file you cannot open, a browser that will not leave a stranger's page, a program you did not install. Close the scare. Do not call the number on it.

title: WhatsApp is not email
description: Chat is a tap on the shoulder. Email is a letter on a desk. Schools, banks, and workplaces still want the letter. Knowing which room you are in saves a week of silence.

title: WhatsApp Web on a computer
description: The green app can sit in a browser. The phone stays the key. Scan once, type with a keyboard, log out when the desk is not yours.

title: When a client goes quiet
description: The work is delivered; the phone goes silent. Chasing payment with dignity: the gentle ladder, the documents that win disputes, the pause of work, and when to walk away.

title: When the cell says ##### or #DIV/0!
description: Hashes are a curtain: the column is too thin. #DIV/0! is divide by empty. #VALUE! is a word where a number should be. The amount is often still there. Widen, or fix the formula, before you panic.

title: When the computer is slow
description: Slow is usually a crowd, a full disk, or a dying drive. Close windows you cannot see. Restart is the polite medicine. A pop-up that sells a “cleaner” is not.

title: When the network is sick
description: The page that will not open has four possible culprits: the device, the radio, the router, the provider. The ladder of checks finds the guilty one in five minutes, without any panic.

title: When the screen stays dark
description: The power light breathes, the fan spins up, but the glass screen stays as dark as midnight. How to test the light, the memory stick, and the TV cord before anybody touches a screwdriver.

title: When there is no sound
description: Silence has a checklist: mute, headphones, the wrong speaker, the player, then the driver. A pop-up “audio fixer” is not on the list.

title: Where the data goes
description: Two gigabytes, finished by Thursday, and you barely watched anything. The four quiet eaters of a bundle, the settings that leash them, and the buying that stops the middlemen.

title: Wi-Fi and the cable under the table
description: Radio is convenient and honest about its limits; copper is rude and fast. Where each one wins, why walls eat the signal, and when to stop fighting and run the cable.

title: Wi‑Fi at home without mystery
description: The router is a small radio. The laptop asks for the house name and the key on the sticker. If the internet dies, check the lights before you blame the website.

title: Wi‑Fi or mobile data — which tap is open
description: The fan is house radio. The arrows are the SIM. Both can be on; one is used. Look at the top of the phone before a video. A download on the wrong tap is a bill.

title: The work that changes and the work that stays
description: An honest look at the fear: transcription changed, judgment did not. The person who can check the machine eats in every season — and where to stand in the decade ahead.

title: Working remote from here: dollars, hours, and the light
description: Remote work is not a hustle, it is a job with a longer commute. The four things it actually demands — proven skill, power and data, written English, and a way to be paid — and how to arrange each.

title: Working with AI assistants
description: The assistant that answers everything and is sure about all of it: how to use the tools as apprentices — drafts, explanations, ideas — and where their confidence must be checked.

title: “You have won” — the message that wants a fee
description: A prize you did not enter is not a prize. A fee to release money is a tap that only flows out. Delete. Do not call the number. Do not send airtime to claim a car.

title: Your first email, sent properly
description: An address, a subject that tells the truth, a body with one job, and the paperclip. Reply is not Reply all. The first message you send should be one you would still sign on paper.

title: Your first hand: from freelancer to small studio
description: The day the work exceeds your hands is a good day with a hard question. Hiring your first person — paying fairly, teaching openly, checking quality, and the arithmetic of two desks.

title: Your first paid client, start to finish
description: One real job, walked the whole way: the enquiry, the written quote, the deposit, the delivery, the invoice, and the ask that turns one client into the next.

title: Your hands on the keyboard
description: Hunt-and-peck works until it does not. Home row, the keys that edit, and the two shortcuts that copy a world. Ten honest minutes a day beats a course you never open.

title: Your judgment stays yours
description: The pilot who lets the autopilot fly alone is the pilot nobody wants. Which skills must stay manual in your own hands, and how to practise them without the crutch on certain days of the week.

title: Zero trust: the gate that trusts nobody
description: What is zero trust security? The old walls trusted whoever was inside. Zero trust trusts nobody — every knock, every time, identity and device both checked. You already carry its front door in your pocket.

title: Zipping a folder to email
description: A zip is a suitcase. Many files become one. Attach the suitcase, not twenty photographs. The other person unzips on their desk.
